---
title: "receive-ticket skill"
format: gfm
---

The first step in the AI-assisted IT ticketing workflow: produce a clean intake summary for a freshly submitted ticket so the next skill can classify and prioritize it.

## Layout

```text
skills/receive-ticket/
├── SKILL.md                    # Claude reads this; tells it what to ask and run
├── README.qmd                  # this file (human docs)
├── install.sh                  # copies SKILL.md + scripts/ → .claude/skills/receive-ticket/
└── scripts/
    └── receive_ticket.py       # argparse CLI + load_ticket_context, build_intake_summary, render_summary, main
```

## Install

```bash
bash skills/receive-ticket/install.sh
```

This copies `SKILL.md` and `scripts/` into `.claude/skills/receive-ticket/`. Restart Claude Code so the skill is picked up.

## Usage through Claude

Just describe what you want:

> "Summarize ticket TKT-00042 for me — I'm about to triage it."

Claude reads `SKILL.md` and runs the script.

## Direct CLI

```bash
uv run python skills/receive-ticket/scripts/receive_ticket.py --ticket-id TKT-00042
```

Optional flags:

- `--data-dir data` (default) — directory containing `raw/`, `processed/`, `dictionaries/`.
- `--out-dir data/working` (default) — where the action log is appended.

The script prints a labeled intake summary and appends one row to `data/working/ticket_action_log.csv`.

## Public functions

- `load_ticket_context(data_dir, ticket_id)` — returns `{"ticket": ..., "customer": ...}` or raises `KeyError` / `LookupError`.
- `build_intake_summary(context)` — pure dict → dict, no IO.
- `render_summary(summary)` — pure dict → str (the printed report).
- `main(argv)` — CLI entrypoint, returns 0 on success, 2 on missing ticket / customer / data file.

See `data/README.md` for the meaning of each ticket and customer column.

## Test

```bash
uv run pytest tests/skills/test_receive_ticket.py -v
```
